steps.text: To make the crepe batter: Place flour, milk, water, eggs, melted butter, and salt into a blender. Blend until smooth and set aside.
To make the filling: Beat confectioners' sugar, cream cheese, lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled griddle or nonstick skillet over medium heat. Pour or scoop batter onto the griddle, using approximately 2 tablespoons for each crepe.
Tip and rotate the pan to spread batter as thinly as possible.
Flip when batter is set and edges begin to brown. Continue cooking until bottom begins to brown. Stack finished crepes on a plate; cover with a damp towel.
Fill each crepe with 1/4 cup sliced strawberries and 1/3 cup cream cheese filling.
Roll up and top with a dollop of cream cheese filling and more sliced strawberries.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Strawberry Crepes
raw_recipe.description: These homemade strawberry crepes, with a sweet and creamy whipped filling and fresh strawberries, are perfect for a special brunch or dessert.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you how to make homemade strawberries-and-cream filled crepes. See the technique to make perfect crepes that will come together in a blender and cook in just a few minutes. Consider the lemon flavored, sweetened cream cheese and fresh strawberries- the icing on the cake.

review.reviewBody:
I fell in love with crepes one year at IHOP when they were offering them seasonally. This is a yummy substitute that fills my craving until it's offered again. I give it four stars though because I found the recipe needed some changes. 
I did the last steps of making the cream cheese filling and whipping the cream first, and I put it in the fridge. I'm glad I did this, because cooking the crepes was VERY time-consuming. 2 tablespoons of batter made the crepes too tiny, even when I did tip the pan every which way. So I upped it to about 4 tablespoons or a little less than 1/4 a cup. I also had to cook it on less than medium heat or else it set too fast before I could spread the batter.
 If I had to change anything about my experience, I would have made sure my husband was home to entertain our 15 month old daughter. Cooking the crepes took so long, let's just say by the time I was done I had a screaming baby, a toy-scattered kitchen, and a messy diaper by the end of it. If I had used 2 Tablespoons of batter each time, I would have been cooking half the day and brunch would have become afternoon dinner. 
Time-consuming-- yes, but it's worth the result-- at least until IHOP brings back the crepes!
This is the best recipe I have tried. The only thing I changed was serving the creamy filling and strawberries on top of french toast. Thanks for the great recipe.

This was fantastic! Use a non stick pan and you don't have to use oil to make the crepes. I also had to make two batches f crepes as the filling is so rich and sweet! I would cut the sugar to about 1/4 - 1/2 cup in the future. I rolled them up without filling and put mapel syrup on these for the little kids.
Everything was the same I used a premade crêpe from my local grocery store and I also melted semi sweet chocolate chips in a double boiler and drizzled over the top, yummy!

First time making crepes and these came out spectacular! I added 1/2 cup of white sugar and the vanilla to the whipping cream when I whipped it and set a little aside to top the crepes with then just cut the powdered sugar in half when combining with the cream cheese. Excellent.

This was really good. I did make a change as I did not have heavy cream and don't cook with it because of cholesterol. I decided to use one of those strawberry yogurt tubes the grandkids eat all the time instead of the cream AND I totally left out all of the sugar. I squeezed the whole tube into my Magic bullet blender and blended it with the cream cheese. it was great.
Fantastic recipe! I used Pillsbury Gluten Free Flour blend (wheat sensitivity) and these were just as good, if not better than what I remember from iHop.

Everyone in my family loved it. Some of my kids like the strawberries a little sweeter, so I mixed 1/4 cup of sugar with my strawberries and let them sit overnight to sweeten the strawberries and bring out the juices. I also cut some fresh strawberries for those who didn't want them as sweet.

I mixed in bananas for some and substituted bananas for some. 

I also added 3/4 cup of cool whip instead of 1/2 cup heavy cream, whipped. This made the filling easier to spread and made it a little less dense.

I kept the leftover batter in the fridge. The next morning I stirred the batter then made more. So if you want to make everything the night before or make it before taking some to a friends house you can.

These were amazing. My family told me that I should open a restaurant. The only changes that I made was that I used blackberries instead of strawberries and I did cut down to 3/4 cup of powdered sugar per the suggestion of other reviews. I used half of the berries to make a blackberry sauce and used the other half whole for inside the crepes an on top as a garnish. OMG...they were amazing.

I am wondering if the people who complained the filling was too sweet didn't put too little of whipped cream in? The ingredients say 1 cup heavy whipping cream, whipped. So, you should have equal to two cups of whipped cream once you've whipped it. If you only add 1 cup of whipped cream, it probably will be too sweet. (Cream doubles in volume when whipped). You can add more whipped cream to cut the sweetness. Also if you don't add the lemon juice and zest, it will taste sweeter. If you use fresh lemon zest and fresh juice from a lemon(not bottled), it will give a lighter lemon taste that is barely there. I thought these were great as written.
So good my favorite also can use any filling with this fresh fruit or I personally love blackberry jam by polaner with blueberry syrup
Absolutely mouthwatering! I turned the heat down and flipped them before they became as dark as the ones in the recipe photos. They were 5-star rated 🤩
Used 3/4c of sugar and that was plenty. Other than that, recipe was delicious and made airy, thin crepes.
Perfect recipe for crepes. Have used it for years.
way to much confection sugar, batter recipe is enough for 5 ,and thats scraping the bowl
Everything tasted great with the ratios provided! Can customize the filling with whatever fruits you like. The wife and kids love these crepes! New favorite!

Super amazing. My husband loved them. I didnt use all the whipped topping I made was too much! Added more lemon to the creamy topping and insides and inused raspberries. I added protien powder to my crepes :)

These are definitely the way to a man’s stomach, my boyfriend absolutely loved them and told me I should start a crepe food truck. Excellent recipe!! Only change I would’ve made personally would be to make the filling less sweet by adding more whipping cream, but only because I don’t have the biggest sweet tooth 🩷

Very easy; just toss the first six ingredients into the blender and blend for a few seconds. Then cook crepes as usual and fill with whatever you wish. I filled mine with ricotta cheese, strawberry jam, butter and powdered sugar. I rolled them up, spread some butter all along the top and more powdered sugar... yum!
